overview: This 286-page file documents mid-1930s American concern about alleged Japanese propaganda, espionage, military reconnaissance, and cultural influence in Hawaiʻi, especially through Japanese-language schools, public education, visiting ships and lecturers, consular networks, and organizations promoting Japanese culture. Much of the correspondence originated with Korean activist Kilsoo Haan (also W. K. Lyhan) and anti-immigration campaigner V. S. McClatchy, whose claims circulated among the State, Navy, Interior, and White House offices and prompted official examination of Helen Gay Pratt’s proposed textbook on Japan. Officials often doubted the reliability or motives of the accusers, yet they still investigated the allegations and privately criticized the textbook as overly sympathetic to Japanese views. The latter half of the file consists largely of Felix M. Keesing’s experimental textbook on the Philippines, covering colonial history, American rule, agrarian society, politics, culture, migration, and nation-building—apparently preserved because it belonged to the same Pacific-area educational project.
interest: The file is especially useful for studying how education, cultural exchange, immigration, and military security became entangled in prewar American perceptions of Japan. It preserves not only sensational allegations but also officials’ private doubts, interagency circulation of claims, repeated copies of advocacy material, and efforts to conceal the State Department’s role in reviewing classroom texts. Its most unusual feature is the extensive Philippine textbook embedded in a nominally Japan-and-Hawaiʻi intelligence file: this provides both a valuable contemporary social survey and evidence that officials evaluated purported Japanese propaganda within a broader experiment in teaching American students about Pacific societies. Historians can therefore use the file to examine Japanese cultural diplomacy, Korean anti-colonial activism, anti-Asian exclusionism, bureaucratic threat assessment, and the racial politics surrounding Hawaiʻi’s proposed statehood.
